about.title: Pico Rivera Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen fast, often in the seconds it takes to cross a wet tile floor, step over a torn mat, or navigate a dim stairwell in a Pico Rivera shopping center or apartment building. What follows can be slow and confusing: pain, missed work, and a property owner who may not want to take responsibility. California law requires proving the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn people about it. That's why what happens right after a fall matters so much, from photos of the hazard to requests for surveillance footage before it's deleted. LawProactive doesn't practice law, but we connect Pico Rivera residents with an independent attorney familiar with local businesses, apartment complexes, and public spaces who can evaluate your situation. There's no cost to get connected, and any attorney you're matched with works on contingency, meaning fees only apply if you recover compensation.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a Pico Rivera Premises Case

items.title: Proving Notice
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to address it. An attorney can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records to support that.

items.title: Preserving Video Before It's Gone
items.desc: Many Pico Rivera businesses and complexes record over surveillance footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of that footage can be critical to your claim.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your recovery can be reduced but not eliminated even if you were partly responsible for the fall. An attorney can help present your case in context.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Pico Rivera?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a city building or park, the deadline is much shorter and requires an earlier claim, so it's wise to act promptly.

items.question: What if the fall happened at a business along Whittier or Rosemead Boulevard?
items.answer: Commercial corridors like these have many retail centers and mixed-use properties, and figuring out which entity is responsible for maintenance can be complicated. An independent attorney can help identify the property owner or manager and gather evidence like maintenance records or prior incident reports.

items.question: Do I need to prove the store or landlord knew about the hazard?
items.answer: Yes, California premises liability law generally requires showing the owner had actual or constructive notice of the dangerous condition. This means documenting things like how long a spill sat unattended, whether lighting was broken, or whether similar complaints had been made before.
